title: Introduce invocation lifecycle timelines and alert holdback
author: Marina Patel
description: Adds a new invocation lifecycle timeline metric set, a lightweight timeline rollup service, frontend timeline panels, and an alert holdback mechanism that suppresses transient spike alerts until invocation cohorts demonstrate persistence. This PR provides end-to-end telemetry from request ingress through kernel queueing, scheduler handoff, token generation phases, and streaming flush. Motivation: many SRE incidents were noisy due to short-lived kernel queue spikes that triggered global SLO alerts. By exposing per-invocation lifecycle step durations and a configurable holdback window that checks cohort persistence and finalization state, we reduce alert churn while preserving time-to-detect for sustained regressions. The work touches the ingestion pipeline, metric schema, the telemetry aggregator, the console UI, and alerting rules. This is intentionally incremental: timeline rollups are sampled and have configurable retention, defaulting to conservative storage budget, and the holdback defaults to 30s to start. Includes synthetic replay harness and perf smoke tests to validate correctness and cost profile.
commits: telemetry: add lifecycle step enums and proto fields
aggregator: implement timeline rollup writer and sampled retention policy
console: add timeline panel and timeline-heatline visualization component
alerts: introduce holdback policy engine and alert evaluator changes
tests: synthetic replay harness and flaky-sample unit tests
ci_notes: Initial CI run failed on aggregator unit test due to race on the rollup buffer; fixed by adding a small lock and retry in rollup_writer_test.go. Flaky e2e streaming smoke retry added to pipeline. All subsequent runs green.
review_comments: Jordan Li: Please add metrics for dropped rollup samples and a small doc on expected storage cost for default sampling rates.
Amira Hassan: The holdback window is useful but we need an emergency bypass toggle for oncall to force immediate alerts while diagnosing live incidents.
Tomas Müller: Frontend visualization looks good, but timeline heatline needs better axis scaling for sub-50ms steps to avoid flattening.
author_responses: Marina Patel: Added dropped_sample counter and documented sampling/retention tradeoffs in telemetry/README.md. Storage estimates included with default config.
Marina Patel: Added oncall emergency bypass via a feature flag and an API guard guarded by RBAC. Documented bypass procedure in ops/runbooks.
Marina Patel: Tweaked frontend axis scaling and added percentile overlay for 50th/95th to preserve visibility of low-latency steps.
release_notes: Introduce invocation lifecycle timelines and alert holdback. New metrics: invocation_lifecycle_step_duration_seconds and invocation_lifecycle_finalized_count. New console panels under Invocation Detail and a holdback engine that reduces alert noise for transient kernel queue spikes. Configurable sampling and retention. Emergency bypass flag available for oncall.
manual_steps: 1) Deploy telemetry proto change and run rollup migrator. 2) Enable sampling config in aggregator config map. 3) Deploy console assets. 4) Update alerting rules with holdback namespace and optionally toggle bypass during initial rollout.
observability_impact: Adds two new metrics families and a sampled timeline rollup stream. Default sampling keeps storage increase under 4 percent of current telemetry footprint. Synthetic replay harness included to validate retention and query performance.
performance_notes: Rollup writer uses batching and sampling to minimize write amplification. Local perf tests show 3 to 6 percent CPU overhead on aggregator under 50k rps and median write latency impact under 5ms per batch.
qa_notes: Included synthetic-replay job that replays representative traffic and asserts that holdback prevents alert firing for transient cohorts shorter than the configured window and allows alerts for persistent regressions. Added unit tests for holdback evaluation logic and aggregator sampling behavior.
security_notes: Emergency bypass is gated by RBAC and requires an explicit oncall flag to be set; holdback state is not persisted across nodes to avoid accidental permanent suppression.
notes_for_release_engineer: Coordinate rollout during low-traffic window. Monitor invocation_lifecycle_finalized_count and dropped_sample metrics. If stored rollup volume exceeds target, reduce sampling pct via aggregator config and redeploy. Ensure runbook for emergency bypass is accessible to oncall.
approvals: Amira Hassan: approved with bypass addendum
